febraioTech.title: FebraioTech
febraioTech.description: A live commerce product with a Next.js storefront and Medusa v2 backend, including inventory-aware product flows, account journeys, checkout integrations, and automated tests.
febraioTech.problem: Build a commerce experience where the public catalog, availability, customer journeys, and checkout remain connected to a real commerce backend instead of static storefront data.
febraioTech.role: Independent full-stack engineering across storefront, commerce backend integration, product flows, local infrastructure, testing, and deployment documentation.
febraioTech.architecture: Next.js and React storefront connected to Medusa v2, PostgreSQL, Redis, object storage, and payment integrations. Docker supports the local service topology.
febraioTech.decisions: Keep commerce rules and inventory authority in the backend; represent unavailable products explicitly; validate external inputs and separate customer-facing UI from operational services.
febraioTech.quality: Unit, integration, and end-to-end test paths are present across the monorepo, using Jest, Vitest, and Playwright where applicable.
febraioTech.deployment: The storefront is publicly accessible. The repository also documents containerized local infrastructure and cloud deployment workflows.
febraioTech.imageAlt: FebraioTech live storefront showing the commerce homepage

manualDosAchados.title: Manual dos Achados
manualDosAchados.description: A live product-comparison and buying-guide platform backed by structured editorial, SEO, topic-discovery, and marketplace-ranking workflows.
manualDosAchados.problem: Turn product research into a maintainable editorial system instead of a collection of manually assembled pages, while keeping commercial transparency visible to readers.
manualDosAchados.role: Full-stack product development across the public experience, content model, backend workflows, marketplace synchronization, and deployment-oriented documentation.
manualDosAchados.architecture: Next.js 16 and React 19 frontend with a Strapi 5 backend and PostgreSQL. Backend services handle structured content, discovery, clustering, scoring, and marketplace ranking synchronization.
manualDosAchados.decisions: Keep editorial governance and automation in the content backend, separate public presentation from workflow orchestration, and expose affiliate context in the reader experience.
manualDosAchados.quality: The frontend and backend are maintained as explicit applications with documented schemas and workflows; public pages provide the verifiable product surface.
manualDosAchados.deployment: The platform is publicly accessible. Source links expose the frontend, with the backend maintained as a separate Strapi application.
manualDosAchados.imageAlt: Manual dos Achados live homepage with product guides and rankings

cryptoAi.title: Crypto AI
cryptoAi.description: A read-only market-research copilot that separates deterministic analysis, risk controls, simulated operations, outcome review, and contextual AI-assisted explanation.
cryptoAi.problem: Make market observations and AI-assisted analysis reviewable over time without letting an LLM replace deterministic rules, create exchange orders, or expose provider credentials to the client.
cryptoAi.role: Full-stack architecture and implementation of the React interface, Express API, persistence, AI integration, validation, safeguards, and controlled demonstration environment.
cryptoAi.architecture: React and Vite frontend connected to an Express API with Prisma and PostgreSQL, public market-data feeds, deterministic analysis layers, and an OpenAI review boundary. Provider secrets remain on the backend.
cryptoAi.decisions: Keep live exchange execution out of scope; let AI explain, block, or reduce a simulated decision but never increase risk; separate analysis, journal, outcome evaluation, and reporting; validate requests with Zod.
cryptoAi.quality: Vitest coverage, request validation, Helmet, rate limiting, and explicit error handling support the API boundary and controlled analysis flows.
cryptoAi.deployment: The source is private. The screenshot comes from a controlled local full-stack fixture using public market data and no real exchange balance.
cryptoAi.imageAlt: Crypto AI read-only spot research dashboard running with controlled data

buildBalance.title: BuildBalance
buildBalance.description: A full-stack financial-management system for construction and renovation projects, with budgets, expenses, suppliers, permissions, reports, and audit events.
buildBalance.problem: Keep project budgets, expenses, supplier records, and financial summaries consistent across multiple collaborators and permission levels.
buildBalance.role: Full-stack implementation of the API, data model, authorization rules, financial calculations, audit trail, and React dashboard.
buildBalance.architecture: NestJS API with Prisma and PostgreSQL, paired with a React and Vite frontend using Redux Toolkit and RTK Query. JWT and project-level roles protect operations.
buildBalance.decisions: Calculate financial totals on the server, enforce role and project authorization at the API boundary, and record auditable domain events instead of trusting client-computed summaries.
buildBalance.quality: Jest coverage and Docker-based infrastructure support repeatable verification. The published screenshot uses demonstration values, not client data or claimed business metrics.
buildBalance.deployment: The public repository documents the system and local container workflow. A public API health endpoint is available; no public frontend or user adoption is claimed.
buildBalance.imageAlt: BuildBalance financial dashboard populated with clearly labeled demonstration data

converseComAmor.title: Converse com Amor
converseComAmor.description: A collaborative training experience with anonymous sessions, private role data, real-time participation, structured content, and a security-focused Supabase model.
converseComAmor.problem: Coordinate multi-participant training rounds while keeping each participant's private information protected and the shared state synchronized.
converseComAmor.role: End-to-end implementation of product flows, Next.js application, Supabase schema and RLS, transactional RPCs, content tooling, testing, and operations documentation.
converseComAmor.architecture: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Supabase PostgreSQL, anonymous authentication, Realtime, row-level security, and server-only maintenance routes.
converseComAmor.decisions: Derive authority from authenticated database membership, protect private reactions with RLS, use transactional RPCs for critical mutations, and keep server secrets out of client bundles.
converseComAmor.quality: The verification workflow covers linting, type checks, content validation, database tests, Playwright E2E, production build, and a post-build client-secret audit.
converseComAmor.deployment: Operations documentation defines separate Vercel and Supabase preview/production environments, explicit migrations, health checks, backup, rollback, and scheduled cleanup. No public URL is claimed.
converseComAmor.imageAlt: Converse com Amor collaborative training application homepage
